summary: Iteration 92 - branded emails. I ran 23/23 new tests against the public URL: email assets, admin preview list and kinds, the guardrail on all 8 preview HTMLs, and 2 real sends to delivered@resend.dev. All passed. The regression suites also passed (44/44): forgot/reset/lockout, viewings, home hub, agency teams, and notification read-state/digest. backend.err.log shows no 'Email send failed', ValueError or Traceback lines from these runs. Frontend at 390x844: the admin tile-emails opens /admin/emails and all 8 email-kind chips render. The subject updates when a chip is tapped (unlock -> 'Your AMASS receipt', digest -> '3 new updates on AMASS today', agency -> invite subject). Inside the iframe, the AMASS logo, the Unsplash hero and the FIXA PRO footer logo all load (naturalWidth > 0). The non-admin agent sees 'Admins only'. No page errors. No deprecated Expo packages found.

minor.issue: The app sends 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800' (checked directly on upstream :8001). Through the preview URL, the Cloudflare/ingress edge replaces it with 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate'. This is the edge, not the app. Check it again on the production domain.

The public origin is learned from the first inbound X-Forwarded-Host/Host header and saved permanently in runtime_state. On a fresh DB (e.g. a new prod deploy), a first request with a forged X-Forwarded-Host could make every later email point its logo URLs at that host. Low risk, because the guardrail still requires https and the value is already set in preview. Suggest setting PUBLIC_API_BASE in prod, or checking the host against an allow-list / *.emergentagent.com / the custom domain.

critical_code_review_comments: All 6 send_email call sites use email_theme.render_email: agency_teams, viewings, receipts, notification_center, auth_security and home_hub. Every email gets the new look.
Email asset route: name is checked against a fixed allow-list (_ASSETS), so path traversal is not possible (tested, 404).
Preview iframe uses sandbox='' with srcDoc, which is safe; the images still load.
uvicorn --reload watches backend/tests/, so editing test files reloads the backend. Keep this in mind for flaky mid-run 502s.
